title: SDK Intake Concierge: scoring rubric for language support, auth flows, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable triage "concierge" rubric that product will use to intake and prioritize SDK and client-library requests from customers and internal teams. Focus areas: (1) Language coverage gaps (bindings / idiomatic shims), (2) Enterprise auth/SSO/rotating token patterns and token refresh ergonomics, (3) Streaming ergonomics (resumability, backpressure, chunking, reconnect semantics). The rubric should be engineer-friendly, map to clear follow-up paths (quick fix / design spike / full project), and surface security/compliance flags for early review.

Scope: non-bug feature requests, commercial/enterprise cadence. Excludes deep runtime work (kernel changes, model infra) unless the request explicitly raises runtime SLO or cost concerns. Deliverables: triage form template, 0-20 scoring matrix with thresholds for Fast-Track / design-spike / roadmap queue, example classified backlog of 8 seed requests, and handoff process to ENG/DES/DS for estimates and gating.

Out-of-scope: individual developer ergonomics unrelated to public SDKs, experimental bindings without customer commitments.
acceptance_criteria: A concise intake form exists and is integrated into the Customer Intake Playbook (Confluence link).
A 0-20 scoring matrix with documented weight for each axis is published and approved by Eng and Design leads.
Three seeded real customer requests are classified and routed using the rubric (fast-track, spike, backlog).
A clear owner and SLA exists for triage responses (48h ack, 10 business days for estimated outcome).
Security-required flags automatically escalate to Security review queue when present.
decision_record: 2026-03-03: Chose a weighted scoring model over simple prioritization buckets to better surface cross-cutting concerns (security, maintenance cost, adoption).
2026-03-05: Decided to treat token rotation / refresh patterns as a separate 'auth ergonomics' axis with mandatory security review if KMS/HSM integration required.
2026-03-10: Agreed to ship an MVP rubric and intake form first; tooling integrations (Zendesk/GH automation) are Phase 2.
notes: Weights proposed: customer_impact(6), adoption_estimate(4), eng_effort(4, inverted), security_risk(3), maintainability(3). Max score = 20.
Proposed fast-track threshold: >=16 and eng_effort <= 5 points (can be delivered in a single sprint).
Suggested routing: Fast-Track -> ENG small PR -> release in next minor; Spike -> 2-week discovery with a design artifact; Backlog -> roadmap bucket with quarterly review.

Example language priorities: Rust (+2 adoption for infra customers), Go (+3 for cloud partners), Kotlin (+1 for Android-heavy customers). These modifiers will be replaced with metrics from SDK usage telemetry post-launch.
